DOCS-TRUTH VERIFIED (WebFetch trino.io/docs/467/sql/select.html) BEFORE WRITING:
  - VERBATIM: 'The default null ordering is `NULLS LAST`, regardless of the ordering direction.'
  - Confirms the direction-INDEPENDENT semantics: BOTH `ORDER BY x` AND `ORDER BY x DESC` default NULLs to the END.
  - To override, write `NULLS FIRST` or `NULLS LAST` explicitly per the syntax: `ORDER BY expression [ ASC | DESC ] [ NULLS { FIRST | LAST } ] [, ...]`.
  - This is DIFFERENT from the Postgres/Oracle 'NULL-as-largest' convention — Trino does not treat NULL as the largest value; it pins NULLs to the end regardless of direction.
  - Run-directive note: prior run-directive forms 'ASC → NULLS LAST, DESC → NULLS FIRST' would be the Oracle/Postgres rule — that is WRONG for Trino. Always verify against the docs, not the directive.
